transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Taylor Nguyen (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Emily Carter (CTO, BlueRiver); Ravi Singh (ML Engineer); Marta Lopez (Security); Jordan Kim (Product)

Summary: Quick walkthrough of Redwood's Model Catalog, how to select open models, benchmark guidance, and the compatibility matrix for BlueRiver's on-prem/VPC constrained workloads. Discussed tradeoffs (latency vs cost), quantization compat, and next steps to run representative benchmarks.

[00:00:05] Taylor (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Taylor, AE on this account, and Samir is our systems/SE who will do the deep-dive. Emily, do you want to kick off with your goals for today?

[00:00:20] Emily (BlueRiver, CTO): Sure thanks, uh hi all. Our objective is to understand how Redwood's model catalog maps to our latency and privacy needs. We run a mix of latency-sensitive triage suggestions and longer reports so we want to pick a model that balances cost and accuracy, and that plays nice with our VPC/on-prem constraints.

[00:00:40] Samir (Redwood SE): Great. We'll demo the catalog in the console, show the benchmark numbers, and then look at the compatibility matrix — which models can run on your Dedicated pools or in private deployments and what quantization options we recommend.

[00:00:56] Ravi (BlueRiver, ML Eng): A couple quick things: we have an internal 800-1,200 token average for prompts, sometimes spiking to 3k. Mostly English, some clinical shorthand. Also interested in embedding fallback for retrieval ops.

[00:01:10] Marta (Security): And from security, we need to confirm KMS integration, audit logs retention, and SOC2 attestation. Also any egress to hosted models is a no-go unless we have contractual controls.

[00:01:25] Taylor: Understood. We'll highlight which models are available for Private deployment and what network controls we support. Okay Samir, over to you for the console.

[00:01:40] [screen share sounds]

[00:01:45] Samir (Redwood SE): All right, opening the Model Catalog. You'll see we surface open models with Redwood-verified performance profiles — the key columns are 'Latency (p50/p95)', 'Throughput (tokens/sec)', 'Memory footprint', and 'Compatibility' which lists hosted/dedicated/private.

[00:02:10] Samir: For BlueRiver's use case I'd call out three model families: Llama derivatives (Llama-2/3 style), Mistral variants, and a few opt-style models. We also include quantized builds (q4, q8) where we have verified behavior.

[00:02:35] Ravi: When you say "verified behavior" — is that Redwood's internal benchmarks, or community?

[00:02:42] Samir: Good question. It's a mix: we run internal microbenchmarks across our reference hardware for latency/throughput, and we also collate community-reported evals. In the catalog each model entry links to the benchmark sheet — you'll see exact configs used.

[00:02:58] Taylor: I'll drop the link in chat now: https://redwood.internal/sheets/benchmarks/BRH-demo (note: internal demo link).

[00:03:08] Jordan (Product): I see the compatibility column. Some models say 'Dedicated only' and others 'Hosted/Dedicated/Private'. What controls that?

[00:03:18] Samir: Two main constraints: licensing/patent terms from model owners, and the model's memory footprint vs our quantization toolchain. Some open models are redistributable so we can package them for private deployments; others have constraints. Also, very large FP16 models might only be practical on Dedicated pools unless you use q4/q8 quantization.

[00:03:40] Marta: On KMS, can you confirm we can use our HSM-backed keys in the Private control plane?

[00:03:47] Samir: Yes — we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping of model artifacts and for data-at-rest encryption. Audit logs include token-level request traces (subject to redaction settings). We'll include the SOC2 + KMS integration doc in the follow-up.

[00:04:05] Emily: Good. Walk me through a concrete example — say Llama-2-70B q4 vs Mistral 8x-32K q4 — for our 1k average prompt workload. Which wins for latency and cost?

[00:04:20] Samir: So quick top-level: Llama-2-70B q4 typically gives higher quality on instruction-following in our evals but consumes more memory and has higher p95 latency. Mistral 8x is more cost-efficient with similar quality on many tasks. In the benchmark sheet you'll see p50~80ms p95~280ms for Mistral on a single Dedicated A100-ish config at 1k; Llama-2-70B q4 p50~120ms p95~420ms for the same. But if you need very tight latency SLOs, we recommend a smaller FP16 model with aggressive KV caching or lower batch sizes.

[00:05:05] Ravi: How deterministic are those p95 numbers when you enable continuous batching and autoscale? Our traffic is spiky.

[00:05:12] Samir: We model p95 using observed distributions; continuous batching helps throughput but can add tail latency. For spiky traffic we have two levers: pre-warmed Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput) and routing policies to prefer lower-latency variants for SLO-critical routes. We can show a routing policy example where critical endpoints hit a smaller model replica, non-critical hit larger cheaper model.

[00:05:36] Taylor: And Redwood Optimize gives suggestions automatically — it'll recommend quantization and batch knobs based on your real traffic patterns once you run the evals.

[00:05:45] Jordan: For embeddings, are you recommending the same models or a separate embedding-optimized family?

[00:05:52] Samir: We usually recommend dedicated embedding models (smaller, optimized for vector quality). The catalog tags embedding-ready models and you can filter by 'embedding AUC' scores that we publish.

[00:06:05] Marta: A quick security/process question: if we run a PoC in Hosted for speed, how do you ensure data retention and egress controls?

[00:06:14] Taylor: Hosted is possible but as you noted earlier, egress and retention need contractual controls. For enterprise customers we offer dedicated tenancy and private deployment (VPC) where data never leaves your VPC. We'll detail the contractual boundaries in the follow-up.

[00:06:30] [15 sec pause / typing]

[00:06:45] Samir: Back to the catalog — here's the compatibility matrix view. Each row is a model build; columns: supported runtimes (hosted/dedicated/private), max sequence length, recommended quantization, approximate GPU mem after quant, and known caveats (e.g., uses custom kernels).

[00:07:05] Samir: Example: Llama-2-70B q4 -> Supported: Dedicated, Private; Max seq len: 4k; recommended quant: q4_m. Estimated 48GB memory footprint (after offloading), caveat: needs attention on KV cache for long sessions.

[00:07:22] Ravi: Can we get a compatibility filter like 'works on our on-prem nodes (48GB A100)'?

[00:07:28] Samir: Yes — the console has a hardware filter; you can add your node profile and it will filter models that meet memory/compute constraints. We'll show you how to add BlueRiver's node spec in the follow-up doc.

[00:07:40] Emily: I want to surface runbook concerns: if we promote a model between Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private, what happens to versioning and fallbacks?

[00:07:50] Samir: Redwood manages model versioning and rollouts. We support canary deploys and automatic fallbacks. Promotion is mostly metadata and configuration — you pin model versions in routes. If a model variant isn't available in a zone, our smart routing can fall back to a compatible variant.

[00:08:05] Taylor: That helps with reliability for production.

[00:08:10] [00:08:10] Jordan: For the benchmarks you run, do you also publish quality/regression metrics? We want not just latency but prompt-specific pass rates.

[00:08:20] Samir: Yes — each model entry links to evals. We publish prompt-set-based accuracy/regression metrics and you can add your eval prompt set to Redwood Optimize so we'll surface regressions over time tied to deploys.

[00:08:35] Ravi: One more: quantization — how safe is q4 for our clinical notes? Any hallucination increase?

[00:08:43] Samir: Quantization can slightly alter behavior; we recommend running your prompt set through q4 and fp16 variants. That's what the 1k-token benchmark PoC will do. We also have quality monitoring and rollback policies if you detect regressions.

[00:09:00] Marta: Are we able to disable telemetry or remove PII from logs?

[00:09:06] Samir: You can configure redaction rules and sampling for logs. In Private deployments all logs can be kept in your infrastructure; for Hosted we offer redaction and retention settings.

[00:09:20] Taylor: Okay let's demo a quick inline benchmark run — Samir, can you kick off a synthetic throughput test for Mistral-8x q4 at 1k?

[00:09:30] Samir: Starting now — this is synthetic, single-replica, batch size 8. p50 = 82ms, p95 = 270ms, tokens/sec = 1,900. (note: demo numbers, synthetic).

[00:09:50] Ravi: Nice. Can you run the same for Llama-2-70B q4?

[00:09:56] Samir: Kicking off... p50 = 125ms, p95 = 410ms, tokens/sec = 1,200. Again synthetic.

[00:10:08] Emily: Those numbers line up with your sheet, good. What's the best next step for us — a PoC?

[00:10:17] Taylor: We recommend a two-week PoC: Redwood sets up a Dedicated pool with 2 pre-warmed nodes, we'll run benchmarks with your prompt set and quant options, and Redwood Optimize will produce tuning suggestions. Then we review quality metrics and recommend a rollout.

[00:10:30] Jordan: Estimated cost for that PoC? We need a ballpark to budget.

[00:10:36] Taylor: Ballpark depends on chosen models and pre-warm size; I'll send a draft pricing for a 2-node 2-week PoC and Dedicated monthly commit options.

[00:10:46] Marta: Contract stuff — we need SOC2 report and a Data Processing Agreement before any hosted data is used.

[00:10:52] Taylor: Absolutely — I'll include SOC2 and DPA in the follow-up packet.

[00:10:58] [brief cross-talk]

[00:11:10] Samir: A couple of operational notes: for long sessions we recommend KV cache warming and prefix caching; Redwood can persist and rehydrate KV caches for private deployments to reduce token cost on repeated prompts.

[00:11:25] Ravi: How hard is it to switch quant profiles in prod?

[00:11:30] Samir: We expose quant profiles as separate model variants; switching is a routing change. We usually do canary traffic to q4 and compare quality metrics, then promote. The console shows diffed evals before you rollout.

[00:11:45] Emily: Ok let's recap and assign next steps.

[00:11:50] Taylor: Recap: 1) Redwood will share model catalog export, compatibility matrix, and SOC2/KMS docs. 2) Samir will run synthetic and then representative prompt-set benchmarks on Llama-2-70B q4 and Mistral-8x q4. 3) BlueRiver will send prompt set and compliance checklist. 4) We'll schedule a pricing follow-up for Dedicated PoC.

[00:12:15] Jordan: Timing — can we aim to have the bench runs and docs by next week?

[00:12:21] Taylor: Yes, Samir, can you commit to running the bench by 2026-04-15?

[00:12:27] Samir: Yes — I'll run the bench and upload the sheet.

[00:12:32] Emily: Great. Anything else on blockers? Marta?

[00:12:35] Marta: We need the DPA and clear statement about logs and KMS. Otherwise good.

[00:12:40] Taylor: We'll include that. I'll send a follow-up email with links and a calendar invite for the pricing review.

[00:12:48] [meeting winds down, small talk 30s]

[00:13:20] Taylor: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and bench links.

[End transcript — remaining portion truncated for brevity]
